clue.text: Homework involving criminal activity?

parts.note: read literally, work done at home; really a crime committed with help from someone on the premises

explanation.surface: A question about school homework that strays into crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A crime carried out by or with the help of an employee or resident of the place robbed is so called.

clue.text: Swimmer managed to get up to start when help arrived laughing

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: managed means ran, as in ran a business

indicators.note: to start means take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone coped until rescuers turned up, laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get up' turns RAN into NAR; 'to start' takes the first letters of 'when help arrived laughing', W, H, A, L.
explanation.definitionFit: The narwhal is an Arctic whale with a long tusk, an ocean swimmer.

clue.text: Not feeling at home in front of hard union crew

parts.note: at home means in, as in staying in
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
to crew a ship is to man it

explanation.surface: Someone feels nothing about a union crew from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front of' just places the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cruel and lacking compassion is described as unfeeling or inhuman.

clue.text: Serving at deuce, finally defeats schools

indicators.note: serving suggests the letters are put to a new use, so they are rearranged
finally means take the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A tennis player serving at deuce finally loses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving' rearranges AT DEUCE into EDUCATE; 'finally' adds S from the end of 'defeats'.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or train them, a synonym in the verb sense.

clue.text: Mystified and taken in by source of blood

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: food taken in has been eaten

explanation.surface: Someone baffled and fooled by a blood donor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' sets B beside EATEN. 'It beats me' means I am baffled.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beaten by a puzzle is to be baffled, unable to work it out.

clue.text: One delivers a learned treatise with gravity and independence on both sides

parts.note: an academic paper is a learned treatise
G is the symbol for gravity in physics
I is a standard abbreviation for independence or independent
both sides are right and left, abbreviated R and L

explanation.surface: Someone presents an academic paper with seriousness and freedom of thought.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl who brings newspapers to houses on a round is one who delivers.

clue.text: Romans fought to capture Spanish leader, achieving demands for money

indicators.note: to capture means one piece is taken inside another
fought suggests a struggle, so the letters are thrown about
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Roman soldiers seize a Spanish chief and hold him for ransom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fought' rearranges ROMANS into RANOMS; 'to capture' puts S, from 'Spanish leader', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ransoms are sums asked for the release of captives.

clue.text: Act sensibly, and live with single wise man

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
one means single
a sage is a wise man

explanation.surface: Advice to behave sensibly and live with a wise companion.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave appropriately to one's years, rather than childishly, is the idiom here.

clue.text: Go out, but call back with a case of toothache

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

indicators.note: the case of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Leaving, but phoning back about toothache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns NAME into EMAN; 'case of toothache' gives TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source.

clue.text: Fabulous musician who reinterpreted her opus

indicators.note: reinterpreted suggests the letters are played in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A legendary musician gave a new reading of a woman's work.
explanation.definitionFit: The lyre player of Greek myth is fabulous in the sense of belonging to fable.

clue.text: Finish without justification for crime

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its last letter

parts.note: a reason is a justification

explanation.surface: Ending something without good cause amounts to a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like a link, but its finish gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country is a serious offence in law.

clue.text: Somehow manage to keep quiet after church, drinking this!

indicators.note: after places the following group behind the church letters
to keep means one piece holds another inside
somehow suggests the letters are rearranged in some way

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: Somehow managing to stay quiet after church, while drinking fizz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges MANAGE into AMAGNE; 'to keep' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue points at the sparkling wine being drunk with 'this'.

clue.text: New arrival from brisbane on a teabreak?

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the following words

explanation.surface: A newcomer from Brisbane arriving at a tea break.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn baby is a new arrival.

clue.text: Gambles on the purpose of chess situations

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: an end is a purpose or aim
games of chance are gambles

explanation.surface: Bets placed on the point of chess positions.
explanation.definitionFit: The final stages of chess games, with few pieces left, are so called.

clue.text: During exercises, have a breather and a swim

indicators.note: during means one piece sits inside another

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercises
a lung is the organ you breathe with

explanation.surface: In a PE class, catch your breath and go swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' suggests a rest, but it is the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A plunge is a dive or dip into water, a quick swim.

clue.text: Run through each deserter captured by the enemy

parts.note: per means each, as in per head

indicators.note: captured by means the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: a foe is the enemy
a rat is one who deserts

explanation.surface: Every deserter is caught by the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce or make holes through something is to perforate it.

clue.text: Killed by flipping piece of cloth (decomposed)!

indicators.note: flipping means the word is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: a rag is a piece of cloth
decomposed means rotted

explanation.surface: Death by a rotten piece of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns RAG into GAR. 'flipping' also reads as a mild British swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: To garrotte is to strangle with a cord or wire, a way of killing.

clue.text: A 19 backing the communist split

parts.note: entry 19 is a cheap popular newspaper, and The Sun is one such British paper

indicators.note: backing means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a red is a communist

explanation.surface: A newspaper supporting the communist causes a split.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn apart into pieces is the sense of the adverb.

clue.text: Oval measuring device?

parts.note: suggests something for measuring an oval shape; really a timer for boiling something oval

explanation.surface: A question about an instrument for measuring ovals.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sand-glass used to time boiling breakfast food is the device.

clue.text: Paper bill in America — cover includes nothing!

parts.note: in American usage a tab is a bill

indicators.note: includes means one piece holds another inside

parts.note: a lid is a cover
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An American bill whose cover contains nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid is a popular newspaper of small page size.

clue.text: Good name in delicate material — have a look!

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside another

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric

explanation.surface: A good brand of fine fabric, worth looking at.
explanation.definitionFit: To glance is to take a brief look.

clue.text: Day spent immersed in a bit of poetry is hardly favourable

indicators.note: immersed in means the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: a verse is a bit of poetry

explanation.surface: A day spent reading poetry is not much fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfavourable or hostile conditions are adverse.

clue.text: House firm on double time — a case of granite!

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: double means the letter appears twice
the case of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A company paying double time for granite work on a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a small country home.

clue.text: Conspicuous apartment accommodating elderly relative

indicators.note: accommodating means holding another piece inside

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
gran is a grandmother, an elderly relative

explanation.surface: A showy flat with room for grandma.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagrant offence is glaring and obvious.

clue.text: Edward took in a couple of pages and fell asleep

indicators.note: took in means one piece contains another

parts.note: Ned is a short form of Edward
PP is the abbreviation for pages, two P's

explanation.surface: Edward read a few pages and nodded off.
explanation.definitionFit: To nap is to take a short sleep, so napped means dozed off.

clue.text: I've a taste for change and will spend the summer in bed

indicators.note: for change means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fancies a change and plans to sleep through summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Some animals pass the hot season dormant, the summer counterpart of hibernation.

clue.text: Type of desk work after lucky streak ended flat

indicators.note: after places the work letters behind the others

parts.note: a gambler on a roll is on a lucky streak

indicators.note: ended means take the last letter of the word

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A gambler's winning run came to a flat end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ended flat' gives T, the last letter of 'flat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk with a sliding slatted cover is a common kind of writing desk.

clue.text: Lost in Burma with one from Italy

indicators.note: lost suggests the letters have wandered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lost in Burma with a companion from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Umbria, a region of central Italy.

clue.text: Hearing of attempt, engineers get an old ship

indicators.note: hearing of means the word sounds like a different spelling

parts.note: a try is an attempt
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: After a trial, the engineers are given an ancient vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient galley with three banks of oars.

clue.text: Questioned legal document covering barrister's instructions

indicators.note: covering means one piece wraps around another

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
a brief is the instructions given to a barrister

explanation.surface: A legal deed wrapped round a barrister's brief was examined.
explanation.definitionFit: To debrief someone is to interview them after a mission.
